## Change control during hypercare (EXT-110-005)

§13.4's emergency path has 6 steps and each has a disposition.
`COMPRESSED` is what "expedited" means and is allowed — with the shortcut named.
`SKIPPED` is refused: a path missing a step is not a fast path, it is a different one.

| Step | Disposition | Shortcut taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| risk | `FULL` | — |
| test | `COMPRESSED` | the full nightly regression was not run; the untested surface is the four unrelated modules |
| approval | `COMPRESSED` | one approver instead of the standing two |
| rollback | `FULL` | — |
| deployment | `FULL` | — |
| evidence | `FULL` | — |

Emergency-change findings: 0.

_no findings_

Configuration-fix findings: 0 over 3 fixes. 1 of 3 configuration fixes bypassed the landscape, of which 0 lack an authorising emergency change or a promotion back.

_no findings_

## Exit and transition criteria (EXT-110-007)

§13.5 says hypercare exits "only when" all 7 hold. It is a conjunction,
not a score — a readiness percentage is what lets six satisfied criteria carry the seventh.

| Criterion | Verdict | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defects` | **SATISFIED** | 3 defect(s) reviewed; no unresolved S0/S1 and no unaccepted S2. |
| `businessCycles` | **SATISFIED** | 3 critical cycle(s) complete or covered. |
| `thresholds` | **SATISFIED** | 7 dimension(s) within threshold for the agreed period. |
| `workarounds` | **SATISFIED** | 5 workaround(s), each complete and either closed or accepted. |
| `handover` | **SATISFIED** | All 11 items accepted by a named owner. |
| `knowledge` | **SATISFIED** | Sessions and simulations passed; 3 seat(s) attested. |
| `signoff` | **SATISFIED** | Signed by customer service owner and Tenure service owner over evidence://hypercare/transition-manifest. |

Verdict: **EXIT**. All 7 of §13.5's criteria are satisfied.

## On-call, escalation and handoff under an outage (EXT-110-010)

7 hypercare seats, drawn from §12.2's list, on a three-window
follow-the-sun rota. §12.2 already requires every seat to declare a backup, an escalation
and a handoff, and `cutover-command-roles.mjs` already refuses a roster that omits them.
What that cannot tell you is whether the declarations WORK — so the outages below are run.

| Outage | At (UTC) | Unavailable | Seat under test | Holder | Route |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `primary-unavailable` | 10:00 | 1 | `identity-lead` | identity-lead-deputy | BACKUP |
| `primary-and-deputy-unavailable` | 10:00 | 2 | `identity-lead` | emea-oncall | ROTA via `08:00–16:00 UTC` |
| `seat-and-rota-unavailable` | 10:00 | 3 | `identity-lead` | incident-commander-primary | ESCALATION via `incident-commander` |
| `night-window` | 03:00 | 2 | `integration-lead` | apac-oncall | ROTA via `00:00–08:00 UTC` |

The drill resolves all 7 seats for all 4 outages — 28 resolutions — because a roster where 6 seats have working cover and the 7th does not passes any sampling.

Unheld seats across the drill: 0.

_no findings_

Coverage lost by the seat under test when its rota window is also out:

- before: 1440 minutes of the 1440-minute day; after: 960; lost: 480 — the EMEA window exactly. A rota with no gaps and one person per window has 24 hours of coverage and zero hours of resilience.

Handoff findings across the drill: 1.

- `held-by-escalation` — "identity-lead" was covered only by escalating to "incident-commander". That is the path working, and it is also a seat with no local cover: §12.2's backup and rota both failed for this outage. Reported rather than refused — an escalation that answers is a pass, and one nobody notices becomes the rota.

rules proves that something refused it rather than that this rule did.
